mark-gonzalez.text: Authored AB 1896 (with Speaker Rivas), the "GTFO Act": bars people who personally engaged in immigration enforcement from becoming California peace officers (effective Jan 1, 2028); applicants must declare prior immigration enforcement. Bill enrolled September 4, 2026.

On his GTFO bill: "If you participated in cruel, baseless immigration enforcement — if you violated civil rights, ignored due process, or followed unlawful orders — You will not be welcomed into California's public workforce."

source.title: State Bill Introduced to Bar ICE Officers from Public Employment - Rafu Shimpo

mark-gonzalez.text: Announcing AB 1896: "They have been targeting people who look like me; people with brown skin." Said he stands with the Speaker on legislation so "we are not going to abandon my community; not ever."

source.title: California's GTFO Act Disqualifies ICE Agents from Local Public Employment - California Globe

mark-gonzalez.text: Principal coauthor of AB 736, the Affordable Housing Bond Act of 2026, authorizing $10 billion in state bonds for affordable housing programs including rental assistance, homeownership, and farmworker housing; amended in Senate June 22, 2026.
Coauthor of AB 804, which would make housing support services (transition navigation, deposits, tenancy support) a covered Medi-Cal benefit for people experiencing or at risk of homelessness.
Coauthor of AB 1109 (Kalra), creating an evidentiary privilege for confidential communications between union agents and the workers they represent.
Coauthor of AB 1331 (Elhawary), restricting employer workplace surveillance tools, e.g. no monitoring in bathrooms; penalties up to $500 per violation. Enrolled September 4, 2026.

Authored AB 2332, requiring the State Department of Education to establish a Dual Language Immersion Coordinator (pending appropriation) to help schools start or expand dual language programs. Approved by Governor September 27, 2026.

Authored AB 817 after the June 2026 Boyle Heights cold storage fire: cold storage facility permits require a contingency fund of up to $20 million for community relief; survivor settlement payments excluded from state income tax. Chaptered September 27, 2026.

Describes himself as "an organizer, a caregiver, a renter, and an activist" who believes "the system isn't working for ordinary people." Priorities listed from his time as LA County Democratic chair: free community college, clean air and water, affordable housing, abortion rights protection.
2024 campaign priorities: raising wages for working families, addressing LA's homelessness and affordability crisis, and guaranteeing healthcare access to all residents.

source.title: Mark Gonzalez triumphs: A new era begins for Assembly District 54 - Los Angeles Blade
